score.note: Correctly distinguishes response-dependent, request-only, and dynamic placeholder expressions, with focused classification and regression tests.
Fixes nested reusable-caller cancellation and wakes blocked runs, with focused tests; its extra refresh path is somewhat more state-dependent than the reference.
It appears to fix staging and cover the listed path cases, but forcing `diff.mnemonicPrefix=false` unnecessarily changes the user’s configured diff presentation.
Implements the requested link-suffix behavior in ZIP and squashfs, keeps listing and lookup consistent, and adds focused coverage, though some ZIP-specific edge cases are not tested directly.
Correctly distinguishes response-data placeholders from request-only expressions, covers direct and shorthand placeholder access plus key lookalike cases, and keeps the changes focused.
Matches the reference fix, synchronizes close and reuse while releasing references once, protects abstract sockets from unlinking, and adds broad regression coverage.
The wrapper correctly reconnects and resets SNMPv3 state, but deferred closure can leave later table requests in the same Gather on the stale session, and the package suite failed.
Implements the requested ZIP and squashfs link behavior with escape-safety coverage; the tests could also explicitly verify range and seek reads.

It handles replayed timestamps and selected/stale chunk release, but marks exemplars only at commit, leaves the ordinary-GC appender retained, and the added tests do not compile because of expressions like `new(int64(150))`.

Preserves exemplar-referenced series identities through GC and WAL replay while reclaiming persisted chunks, with focused tests covering both appender APIs, compaction modes, restarts, and concurrent appends.
Implements link handling for both backends with strong range, lookup, and copy-safety tests, but ZIP clash filtering can drop a valid symlink when names overlap through the `.rclonelink` suffix.
It implements the requested close-and-reset recovery with useful coverage, but the package suite failure and unrelated Gosmi test-path change reduce confidence and scope.

It distinguishes actual response-data placeholder references from request-only expressions and adds focused coverage for shorthand and direct calls, escaped literals, similar names, and dynamic names.

Implements the requested link handling across ZIP and squashfs with safe-copy coverage and documentation; the tests are strong but do not directly verify range/seek reads or successful symlink recreation.
Matches the reference fix and adds focused coverage for immediate cleanup, reference counting, double close, relisten races, and abstract sockets.
It preserves series identity through the WAL replay cutoff while reclaiming eligible chunks, and adds broad coverage for compaction paths, restart replay, both appender APIs, and concurrent appends.

The generalized parser and primary diff paths are solid, but `stash show` remains unprotected and the CLI-prefix workaround is not tested against `diff.noprefix`, leaving the broader prefix guarantee incomplete.
The taskless-caller re-aggregation addresses nested cancellation and runner acknowledgement, with strong regression coverage; unconditional settling and emission are somewhat broader than necessary.

It generalizes header-path parsing and configures parseable prefixes for most relevant commands, but disables mnemonic prefixes and omits the DiffIndexCmdObj override, leaving a config-sensitive path uncovered.
Matches the reference fix and updates command-argument assertions; direct tests for the parser edge cases are not apparent in the shown patch.

Matches the reference behavior across ZIP and squashfs, with focused coverage including hostile-link copying; tests could additionally exercise ranged reads and lookup behavior when links are disabled.
The refactor targets the requested lifecycle cases, but it fails the package suite and all seven hidden checks, so it cannot be considered a working fix.

It addresses both reported paths and tests nested acknowledgements plus waiter rechecks, but caller status relies on a direct-child snapshot and readiness checks run even when the run status did not change.
Implements the reference fix with synchronized reference-counted closes, protects abstract sockets, and adds focused coverage for cleanup, double closes, reuse, and relisten races.
Tracks literal and dynamic CEL placeholder references to distinguish response-driven retries, with focused tests for the specified cases.
Implements the required close-and-reset reconnect path with useful coverage, but also adds unrelated MIB-loader behavior and tests.

It implements the close-and-reconnect flow and adds useful coverage, but restores nonempty configured USM engine values instead of always forcing discovery, includes an unrelated gosmi test edit, and the package suite fails.
Implements the reference lifecycle fix and adds focused coverage for reference counts, repeated closes, relistening races, datagrams, and abstract sockets.
It implements the intended prefix handling and section-path fallbacks across the relevant Git commands, with useful command-argument test updates and no apparent scope creep.
The caller aggregation and force-cancel wakeup paths are sound and focused; tests cover direct callers but not nested callers, and the no-update emission is broader than necessary.
The caller re-aggregation and run-settlement wakeup cover the reported paths, with minor over-reporting of unchanged callers and unnecessary wake checks on no-op cancellations.
The response-placeholder detection and regression coverage match the requested behavior; the exported Placeholders method could clone its slice to avoid exposing mutable internal state.
The retention snapshot misses accepted exemplars still awaiting commit, so compaction can still remove their series reference; the package test suite also fails.
The recovery path closely matches the reference and adds useful reconnect/close coverage, but the package suite fails and the unrelated gosmi test adjustment broadens scope.

The wrapper correctly resets stale SNMPv3 state and reconnects closed sessions, but the plugin delays closing until all table work finishes, includes unrelated gosmi-test edits, and the package suite is reported failing.
The deepest-first caller refresh and run wakeup address both reported failures, though the wakeup condition is broader than necessary and may cause redundant emitter checks.
The patch targets the relevant GC and restart scenarios, but its bespoke chunk-release path is not yet reliable: the TSDB package suite fails and none of the hidden cases pass.
Implements the requested ZIP and squashfs symlink behavior with consistent lookup, range-aware reads, safety coverage, and focused tests and documentation.
Implements suffix-based symlink exposure, target reads and ranges, copying, and ZIP containment with strong tests, though squashfs lookup and filtering are less comprehensive than the ZIP path.
Tracks literal CEL placeholder references, including direct `ph` calls, distinguishes response placeholders from request-only expressions, and adds focused regression coverage for both behaviors.
Matches the reference lifecycle fix and adds focused coverage for reference counting, double close, close/relisten races, and abstract sockets.
The parser and primary staging paths are well covered, but the stash-show diff call site is missed and remains vulnerable to the same prefix configuration.

It fixes prefix handling and ensures generated patches are parseable, but forcing diff.mnemonicPrefix=false needlessly discards the user’s requested prefixes, and the visible tests mostly assert command arguments.

It handles replay retention, chunk release, and many restart/cutoff cases, but records exemplars only at commit and accesses the packed pending-commit state non-atomically, leaving concurrent append and GC paths vulnerable.
The production changes implement the required close-and-fresh-engine-discovery path, but the reported package-suite failure and unrelated test-path edit weaken confidence and scope.
The main symlink flows and copy-safety cases are handled well, but the collision filter can omit a legitimate regular `.rclonelink` member when its unsuffixed path exists.
The implementation addresses the prefix and header-parsing cases comprehensively; the visible test updates mainly verify command arguments rather than exercising the parser edge cases.

The patch handles nested caller cancellation, run-status refresh, and concurrency rechecks with strong targeted tests, though it reports unchanged callers as updated and emits a run recheck even when cancellation did not settle the run.
Storage-backed retention covers compaction, replay, snapshots, and both appender APIs, but can miss an exemplar queued in an uncommitted appender before it reaches storage.
The ref-counting approach is relevant, but the package suite fails and the unconditional `@` check misclassifies filesystem paths on non-Linux systems.
The storage-based retention covers the requested GC, restart, and chunk-lifecycle cases, but can miss an exemplar queued by an appender before it is committed to circular storage.
